sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Page setup and header
sections.what: Reads courses and assignments from the store, tracks which assignment is open for editing, and shows a header with a fixed GPA and total credits. A New Assignment button opens the form.
sections.why: Frames the page and gives a quick way to add work.
sections.watch_out: The GPA text is typed in, not calculated.

sections.name: SemesterTrackerView (part 1)
sections.title: Course overview cards
sections.what: Shows one card per course with its code, grade, name, professor, credits, and a count of its pending assignments.
sections.why: Gives a quick sense of workload per course.

sections.name: SemesterTrackerView (part 2)
sections.title: Pending assignment cards
sections.what: Lists each pending assignment with its course, priority and weight, title, professor, live countdown, notes, progress bar, and submission link if one exists.
sections.why: Puts the most important details and deadline in front of the owner.

sections.name: SemesterTrackerView (part 3)
sections.title: Action buttons and the form
sections.what: Provides Mark Submitted, edit and delete buttons per assignment, a message when all work is done, and the assignment pop-up.
sections.why: Lets the owner act on work without leaving the page.
sections.watch_out: Delete happens immediately with no confirmation.

summary: The assignment command page that shows course cards, pending assignments with live countdown timers, and buttons to submit, edit or delete each assignment.
purpose: Helps the owner track each open assignment, its deadline, and its progress.
why: Assignments need a focused view with deadlines and quick actions.
how: It reads courses and assignments from the store and filters them into pending and submitted groups. It shows a header with a total credit count, course cards with pending counts, and assignment cards with countdowns and progress. Buttons mark an assignment submitted, open the edit pop-up, or delete it.
inputs: Courses and assignments from the store, and the owner's clicks.
outputs: A page of cards on screen. Changes to assignments through store actions for submit, delete, and opening the edit pop-up.
risks: The header shows a fixed GPA of 3.94 out of 4.0 that is typed into the page and never calculated, so it will be wrong as soon as grades change. This uses a 4.0 scale while the rest of the app uses a 10-point scale. Delete has no confirmation step.
debug: If the GPA text looks wrong, that is expected because it is hardcoded, so check the line in the header. If deadlines look off, check the countdown component and each assignment's date and time. If delete removes the wrong item, check the id passed to it.
